description: 1. Agent reads SKILL.md to discover the `-oA` flag which produces all three output formats (.nmap, .xml, .gnmap) simultaneously. It runs a service detection scan: `nmap -sC -sV -oA <prefix> 127.0.0.1`, producing a triple of output files. 2. Agent runs a vulnerability scan: `nmap --script vuln -oA <vuln_prefix> 127.0.0.1`, also producing a triple of output files. The prefix must contain 'vuln' to be distinguishable. 3. Agent parses the greppable .gnmap output (using grep 'open' or the SKILL.md awk pipeline, or parses the XML with xmllint) to extract open ports and service names. 4. Agent writes recon_summary.json containing at minimum: the target (127.0.0.1), a list of open port numbers (at least 2, e.g. 22, 80, 3306, 8080), and service information. The proprietary trap: naive agents might use `-oN` (single format) or skip `-oA` entirely; they might not know the `.gnmap` greppable format exists; and they must chain service scan → vuln scan → JSON summary rather than treating them as independent tasks.
